proposal.hypothesis: A flattened, statically scheduled pixel loop should expose enough independent work while preserving contiguous pixel writes and avoiding per-iteration scheduler overhead. A direct serial path at one requested thread avoids OpenMP team overhead in the 1-core case. Pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams should make the same uniform sequence recur for a given seed and pixel regardless of scheduling or thread count.

retained: Replace shared drand48 state with a SplitMix64 stream initialized from the input seed and linear pixel index; each pixel advances only its local stream.
Flatten the image to a pixel-index loop with static OpenMP scheduling and num_threads bounded by the requested thread count; execute serially when one thread is requested.
Preserve the primary-ray and ambient-ray loops, intersection geometry, and per-pixel accumulation order; each iteration writes only its own RGB triplet.

proposal.hypothesis: A dynamic pixel schedule with chunks of 64 should balance spatially varying hit and ambient-occlusion work better than a static contiguous partition while keeping scheduling overhead bounded. Per-pixel SplitMix64 streams seeded from one serial draw should make samples independent of worker scheduling and thread count; the one-worker path avoids OpenMP overhead.

retained: Initialize one render seed serially from the caller's drand48 state, then derive independent per-pixel SplitMix64 streams.
Parallelize flattened pixel iterations with OpenMP dynamic scheduling in 64-pixel chunks and request no more than the supplied worker count.
Keep a direct serial loop for the one-worker case and preserve the primary sample and ambient-ray loop counts.
